items.name: Configuration manager
items.description: Static: service layer; owns the configuration table SWC-SUP-050 (four supervised tasks T_IN, T_CTRL, T_OUT at 10 ms and T_DIAG at 100 ms, release order T_IN, T_CTRL, T_OUT, T_DIAG after T_OUT in every tenth period, start limit 2 ms for all four, execution limit 3 ms for the three 10 ms tasks and 20 ms for T_DIAG) and validates it once at start-up; the supervisor code reads every task, period, limit and order from the table so a change of data needs no change of code. Uses SWC-SUP-031 to notify faults and SWC-SUP-036 for the memory read access. Dynamic: called by the start-up manager SWC-SUP-002 in the start-up task SWC-SUP-060 after the integrity checks; a limit longer than its task period, a zero period, an unknown task, or a period that the scheduler cannot realise (DEC-SWC-015: a period that is not a whole multiple of the 10 ms tick, or whose tick count does not fit the scheduler's per-entry tick counter) makes it notify fault code 9 (entity CONFIG) through SWC-SUP-031, so accepted configuration data always has the timing it specifies, after which the fault manager latches the safe state; the table is read-only after a successful validation.

attributes.safe_state: invalid configuration -> fault code 9 -> latched safe state (SWC-SUP-008)
attributes.memory: configuration table static, size set by the four-task set; no dynamic allocation

items.name: Start-up manager
items.description: Static: application layer; sequences everything after a reset and owns the reset-control resource (RCC reset flags and reset request, driver interface SWC-SUP-025). Uses SWC-SUP-036 (output control), SWC-SUP-025, SWC-SUP-033 (CRC), SWC-SUP-037 (memory read access), SWC-SUP-001 (configuration validation), SWC-SUP-039 (reports), SWC-SUP-031, SWC-SUP-032, SWC-SUP-035 (watchdog control) and SWC-SUP-038 (reset request service it provides). Dynamic: runs once in the start-up task SWC-SUP-060 in this order: (1) configure the two control outputs and the status signal as outputs driven low, before any other step, leaving them inputs until then; (2) classify the reset cause from the reset flags as POR, IWDG, WWDG, SW or OTHER; (3) request the start-up message RST,<cause> through SWC-SUP-039 within 10 ms of the classification instant; (4) when the cause is IWDG or WWDG report fault code 8 with entity IWDG or WWDG after the RST message through SWC-SUP-031 (also when the watchdog reset interrupted the handling of an earlier fault); a code 8 report counts toward the latch rule when it is made (at the report completion, SWC-SUP-008), does not itself enter the safe state and does not stop the start-up; (5) while the safe-state latch is set never release a task, never drive the status signal high and stay in start-up; (6) otherwise compute CRC-32/MPEG-2 over __app_start..__app_end and compare with the word at __app_crc (mismatch -> fault code 5, entity CODE), then over __cfg_start..__cfg_end against __cfg_crc (mismatch -> fault code 6, entity CONFIG), both before any task is released, each CRC run being cut into chunks with an independent-watchdog service between chunks (DEC-SWC-004); (7) validate the configuration through SWC-SUP-001; (7a) report-completion barrier: when a code 8 report was requested in step 4, do not evaluate the latch in step 8 until SWC-SUP-011 has given the completion notification or the failure notification of that report through SWC-SUP-039 (the code 8 count and the third-report latch decision of SWC-SUP-008 are taken at that completion, in one critical section); until then the start-up task keeps driving the transmit step and servicing the independent watchdog between steps (DEC-SWC-004, DEC-SWC-011); the wait is bounded because a transmission that makes no progress stops the independent-watchdog service, so the watchdog resets (the code 8 count was not advanced for the interrupted report); a failure notification means no report was made and the latch stays as it is; (8) after step 7a, when both checks passed (no code 5 or code 6 fault in step 6, no configuration fault in step 7) and the latch, re-read after step 7a, is clear, call the output control to drive the status signal high, start alive supervision in SWC-SUP-006 and permit the scheduler SWC-SUP-005 to release tasks; a code 8 report made in step 4 is not a fault that prevents start-up and does not hold back status-high or task release by itself, only a set latch does, and the latch is read only after the code 8 report has completed (step 7a), so a third code 8 report that sets the latch always does so before any task release or status-high (SWR-LAT-004, SWR-LAT-010, SWR-LAT-011, SWR-SAF-004, SWR-SAF-006). A fault of code 1 to 7 detected in steps 6 or 7 stops the sequence: no task is released and no status-high is requested. The independent-watchdog service intervals of start-up are bounded by DEC-SWC-004; the window watchdog is enabled only by the first control cycle (DEC-SWC-005).

attributes.safe_state: start-up fault (code 1 to 7, steps 6 or 7) or set latch -> no task released, outputs and status signal low; a code 8 report alone does not prevent start-up
attributes.memory: chunk cursor and CRC context in start-up stack frame only (no dynamic allocation)

items.name: CRC-32/MPEG-2 engine
items.description: Static: service layer; pure software computation of CRC-32/MPEG-2 (polynomial 0x04C11DB7, initial value 0xFFFFFFFF, no reflection, no final XOR, bytes in increasing address order), written in C11 without dynamic memory or recursion. It is stateless: the running CRC value lives in a context object owned by the caller, so one value over a whole range can be produced from consecutive chunks or segments. It touches no register (the CRC peripheral is not used by this architecture, DEC-SWC-006). Provides SWC-SUP-033. Dynamic: called by the start-up manager (whole ranges in chunks, in the start-up task) and by the run-time checker (one segment per control cycle); it never blocks, is bounded by the length of the byte range passed, and has no error path other than a null or zero-length input, which returns the unchanged context.

attributes.memory: no static state; context object (one 32 bit value) provided by caller

items.name: Run-time code integrity checker
items.description: Static: application layer; owns the run-time check state SWC-SUP-053 (segment cursor and running CRC context). Uses SWC-SUP-033 (CRC), SWC-SUP-037 (memory read access) and SWC-SUP-031 (fault notification). Dynamic: called once per control cycle by the control-cycle task SWC-SUP-061 after the program flow check; processes the range __app_start..__app_end (excluding the end byte; at most 1 MiB) one segment per cycle in increasing address order, each segment 1 KiB except the last segment of an image whose length is not a multiple of 1 KiB (remaining bytes only), the first segment of the next pass following the last segment of the previous pass; the running CRC context is initialised to 0xFFFFFFFF at the first segment of a pass and carried unchanged from segment to segment, so that one whole-range CRC is determined at the end of a pass; at the end of a pass it compares with the word at __app_crc and on mismatch notifies fault code 7 (entity CODE). Its processor time is at most 0.5 ms per control cycle (task budget in SWC-SUP-061); one segment per 10 ms cycle gives a pass over 1 MiB (1024 segments) in 10.24 s, within the 11 s limit. The image length is limited to 1 MiB by the link (design constraint, verified by inspection); no state is reset between segments within a pass.

attributes.safe_state: run-time CRC mismatch -> fault code 7 -> fault manager reaction
attributes.memory: cursor and one 32 bit CRC context; segment bytes read in place from flash, no copy

items.name: Task scheduler
items.description: Static: application layer; the timer-driven scheduler that releases the supervised tasks. Reads the configuration table SWC-SUP-050 (read-only) and uses the task interface SWC-SUP-030, the time service interface SWC-SUP-034 and the fault state interface SWC-SUP-032. Provides SWC-SUP-030 towards the supervised application tasks. Dynamic: called by the control-cycle task SWC-SUP-061 at each 10 ms tick (the time base, CON-SUP-006). The task set, each task's period and the release order are not coded in the scheduler: at each tick it walks the validated configuration table SWC-SUP-050 in its configured release order, and releases every task whose configured period has elapsed in ticks since its previous release (a tick counter per table entry, kept by the scheduler in its own state; the number of entries is the configured task count). The scheduler holds no task name, period or order of its own, so a change of the task set, a period or the order is a change of configuration data only (SWR-CFG-007). Default configuration (SWR-CFG-002, SWR-CFG-003): four tasks, T_IN, T_CTRL and T_OUT with a period of one tick released in this order every cycle, and T_DIAG released after T_OUT in every tenth cycle; the default is data in SWC-SUP-050, not scheduler logic. Period granularity (DEC-SWC-015): a configured period is a whole number of 10 ms ticks, at least one, and the tick count fits the per-entry tick counter; start-up validation (SWC-SUP-001) rejects any other period as a configuration fault, so the scheduler never has to round a period. Only a configuration that start-up validation accepted is used; a configuration fault (fault code 9) leaves the safe-state latch set so no release happens (SWR-CFG-009). The scheduler records the release instant of each released task for the timing supervisor; before the first release it requires the permission of the start-up manager (both start-up checks passed) and never releases any task while the safe-state latch is set (also after a software or watchdog reset and after the checks passed), nor after a fault has been detected until the next reset (no release is bounded by the supervisor, the tasks only run in a released cycle). Has no blocking operation.

items.name: Timing supervision
items.description: Static: application layer; owns the per-task supervision state SWC-SUP-051 (last release instant, start instant, completion instant, consecutive-period counter). Uses SWC-SUP-034 (time base, unit 10 us), SWC-SUP-030 (events) and SWC-SUP-031 (fault notification). Dynamic: receives release, start and completion events from SWC-SUP-005 and the tasks through SWC-SUP-030; the timer compare event handler SWC-SUP-062 invokes it at the start-limit expiry and at the execution-limit expiry of every released task, so a deadline is detected no later than 100 us after it expires and not at the next 10 ms tick. Alive: a task with no completed execution for 2 consecutive periods of its own -> fault code 1 (entity = task name). Alive evaluation is event driven by the release event, not by a timer compare event: the period of a task ends where its next release begins, so the scheduler SWC-SUP-005, running in the control-cycle task SWC-SUP-061 at the 10 ms tick, delivers the release event of a task through SWC-SUP-030 and this component evaluates that task's alive counter in the same call, before the scheduler records the new release instant and before the task is released. Evaluation at release event of task X, inside the critical section of DEC-SWC-007: (a) if alive supervision is not yet switched on, only the release instant is recorded and the counter stays 0; (b) otherwise, a period is counted as completed when SWC-SUP-051 holds a completion instant of X that is later than or equal to the release instant stored for X's previous release, i.e. an execution of X completed within the period that is now ending; (c) if completed, the consecutive-period counter of X is set to 0; if not completed, it is incremented by 1; (d) when the counter reaches 2 it raises fault code 1 with entity = task name through SWC-SUP-031 (fault manager SWC-SUP-008) once; the scheduler does not release any further task after a detected fault (SWC-SUP-005), so no repeated notification follows. The first release after switch-on has no previous release instant and only starts the period, it counts neither as completed nor as missed. Elapsed periods are therefore counted in the unit of a task's own period (one release event per period of the configured period in ticks), not in wall-clock ticks, so a task configured with a longer period such as T_DIAG (every tenth cycle) is evaluated at its own releases only. The maximum detection delay for an alive fault is the end of the second missed period, which is the release event at the 10 ms tick that begins the third period; the detection time bound of 100 us applies to the start and execution limits only and is not claimed for alive supervision. The completion event only stores the completion instant; it does not evaluate the alive counter. Late start: measured start delay (100 us resolution) greater than the configured start limit -> fault code 2; equal is within the limit. Overrun: measured execution time (100 us resolution) greater than the execution limit -> fault code 3; equal is within. Each notification goes to SWC-SUP-031 with its code and the task name; alive supervision is switched on only when the start-up manager reports both integrity checks passed (evaluation rule at the release event above). Detection is a comparison of stored instants against the configured limits, in time-base units U (10 us, DEC-SWC-012), with the rule that a measured value equal to the limit is within it (SWR-TIM-003, SWR-TIM-004). Mechanism and latency bound (DEC-SWC-012): the time base of SWC-SUP-012 has a unit U of 10 us (finer than the 100 us measurement resolution, which is therefore still met; whole 100 us values are derived from it). The configured limit expires at E = release instant + limit (start limit) or start instant + limit (execution limit). A measured value equal to the limit is within it, so the violation condition (measured value greater than the limit) first holds at E + U. There is one compare event per limit, armed by SWC-SUP-012 at E + U when the task is released (start limit) or has started (execution limit); the equality instant E is never decisive and no event is armed there. The handler SWC-SUP-062 is the highest-priority context; its latency from the compare instant to the end of the decision of a single event is at most L1 = 50 us (at most 20 us waiting for an open critical section of DEC-SWC-007, 10 us entry and exit, 20 us for the first decision with the fault reaction; budget in SWC-SUP-062). Coincident or overlapping compare events (DEC-SWC-017): the handler is one pass that decides every compare event due at or before its current time, in expiry order and for equal instants in configured release order, start-limit events before execution-limit events, and re-reads the time before it ends, so an event that falls due during the pass is decided in the same pass; the cycle-end event is taken last. At most one start-limit and one execution-limit event are armed per task at any time (start-up validation SWC-SUP-001 rejects a limit longer than its period, and a task is released once per period), so at most 2N = 8 limit events (N = 4, the capacity of SWC-SUP-051) can be pending together. After the first reaction (outputs low, watchdog inhibited, which are idempotent and are not repeated because their flags are already set) each further decision costs at most 5 us (comparison of stored instants, detection count, write of the pending report cell). The last of eight coincident events is therefore decided at most 20 + 10 + 20 + 7 x 5 = 85 us after the compare instant, so detection is at most U + 85 = 95 us after its limit expires, within the 100 us of SWR-TIM-001 and SWR-TIM-002; a single event is detected at most U + 50 = 60 us after expiry. The 5 us and 20 us values are allocations whose feasibility depends on the open platform clock (OP-SWC-012). A measured value equal to the limit is never flagged (SWR-TIM-003, SWR-TIM-004). The achievability of the 10 us unit at the timer clock is OP-SWC-014. Late-start and overrun decisions from stored instants, independent of when the compare handler runs: every start and completion event is stamped with the time base (unit U) of SWC-SUP-034 inside the critical section of DEC-SWC-007 and the instant is stored in SWC-SUP-051 (it is never discarded). The start event computes start instant minus release instant: if the result is greater than the start limit it raises fault code 2 itself (a late start that occurs before the compare handler has run is reported at the start event); if it is less than or equal to the limit it is within it. The completion event computes completion instant minus start instant and raises fault code 3 itself if the result is greater than the execution limit, otherwise it is within. Only the event that decided cancels the pending compare event of that limit, through SWC-SUP-012, which returns whether the event was still pending; an event that finds its compare event no longer pending (the handler already ran and decided) raises nothing, so each violation is reported exactly once. The compare handler at E + U reads SWC-SUP-051 in the same critical section: if no start instant is stored for the release (late start) or no completion instant is stored for the started execution (overrun), it raises fault code 2 or 3 at once; if an instant is stored, the start or completion event has already decided and the handler raises nothing. Event ordering: a start or completion stamped at or before E precedes the compare event at E + U, so an instant at or before the limit is within it. Each decision uses the stored instants, not an event count, so a late, merged or repeated compare event gives the same result.

attributes.safe_state: detection -> notification to the fault manager, which enters the safe state
attributes.reentrancy: called from task context (events, cycle) and from the timer handler; state updates are protected by the short critical section of DEC-SWC-007
attributes.memory: four task entries of a few 32 bit words each

items.name: Program flow supervision
items.description: Static: application layer; owns the checkpoint log SWC-SUP-052 of the current control cycle. Uses SWC-SUP-030 (checkpoints, configured release order) and SWC-SUP-031. Dynamic: the supervised tasks report one checkpoint each through SWC-SUP-030 during the cycle; the control-cycle task SWC-SUP-061 calls the flow check at the end of each control cycle, which compares the checkpoints of the tasks released in that cycle with the configured release order; when one is missing or arrives out of order it notifies fault code 4 once for that cycle, with the entity being the task expected at the first position at which the received checkpoint differs from the configured order or is missing (no entity task name for other positions), and the log is cleared for the next cycle.

attributes.memory: one entry per released task per cycle

items.name: Fault manager
items.description: Static: application layer; the single place that receives every fault detection (SWC-SUP-031), owns the retained fault state SWC-SUP-054 (safe-state latch, per-code detection counts, eight-entry fault history, fault count since the last power-on reset) and its retained storage driver interface SWC-SUP-026, and the fault-free operating time counter. Provides SWC-SUP-031 and SWC-SUP-032. Uses SWC-SUP-036 (outputs), SWC-SUP-035 (watchdog inhibit), SWC-SUP-039 (report), SWC-SUP-034 (time), SWC-SUP-038 (reset request). Dynamic, two separate handling paths selected by fault code. Path A, codes 1 to 7 and 9 (executed synchronously in the detector's context, in this order): count the detection of that code (detection count only), command the control outputs and the status signal low through SWC-SUP-036 (within 49 ms of the instant the fault becomes detectable; in practice within the detector's execution), inhibit watchdog servicing from that instant until the next reset (SWC-SUP-035), and submit the fault report (SWC-SUP-039, within 10 ms of detection). Path B, code 8 only (raised once at start-up when the reset cause is a watchdog reset): submit the code 8 report (SWC-SUP-039, within 10 ms of the instant start-up classified the reset cause) and do not touch the code 8 count at detection; the code 8 count is advanced only at the report event of that report (below), because SWR-LAT-012 counts a code 8 as a detection when its report is made; path B never commands the outputs low, never inhibits watchdog servicing (SWC-SUP-035 is not called, so servicing continues), never requests a reset and never changes the reported state, and start-up continues; its only reaction is at the report event (below): the code 8 count is incremented by one at that event and, when the incremented value is the third counted since that count was last zero (SWR-LAT-004), the latch is set, all in the same critical section of DEC-SWC-007 as the history append (the latch command then drives the outputs low through SWC-SUP-036 as the held state of SWR-SAF-005, and watchdog servicing is withheld only from that latch set on). Code 8 report not completed: if a reset interrupts the transmission before the completion notification, no code 8 report is made, so the code 8 count is not incremented, the latch is not set for it, no history entry is added and the fault count is not incremented; start-up classifies the reset cause again and raises code 8 again, and each completed code 8 report adds exactly one to the count, so the latch is set only at the completion of the third completed report since the count was last zero, never after fewer than three; a power-on reset first clears counts and latch. If the report line reports a failure (no completion), the same handling applies: no count, no latch, until a code 8 report completes. Report event: a fault report is made when the report completion notification from SWC-SUP-011 for that fault arrives (report line fully handed to the diagnostic line); at that event, in one critical section of DEC-SWC-007, the history entry (code, entity, millisecond stamp taken at the instant of detection, for code 8 at the instant start-up classified the reset cause) is appended, replacing the oldest entry when eight are held, and the fault count since the last power-on reset is incremented by one. Detection counts for codes 1 to 7 and 9, and the latch for codes 1 to 7 (third detection) and 9, are updated at detection, not at the report event; history, fault count, the code 8 count and the code 8 latch are updated only at the report event. A fault whose handling is interrupted by a watchdog reset before report and safe-state entry complete has no report made, so no history entry is added and the fault count is not incremented for it (for codes 1 to 7 and 9 its detection count remains, as it survives the reset); only the code 8 report made at the next start-up adds a history entry and increments the fault count. Per code: for codes 1 to 7 the first or second detection (counted since the count was last zero) requests a software reset within 20 ms after the later of report completion and safe-state entry (completion notification from SWC-SUP-011) provided no watchdog reset came first; the third detection sets the latch (held to the next power-on reset) and requests no reset; code 9 at start-up sets the latch. Counts are separate per code; during operation a count returns to zero only after 60 s of fault-free time in the OPERATIONAL state since the latest detection of any code (a software or watchdog reset never clears it; a power-on reset always clears all counts, see below), the fault-free time being accumulated per control cycle from SWC-SUP-034 with an under-count of at most 100 us per update and at most 10 ms per reset and never an over-count; at a power-on reset (reset cause classified as power-on at start-up) it clears the safe-state latch, all nine per-code detection counts and the fault history as SWR-LAT-009 requires, before any detection is counted; latch, counts and history survive software and watchdog resets. States STARTUP, OPERATIONAL, SAFE and LATCHED are derived here (LATCHED has priority) and provided through SWC-SUP-032.

attributes.safe_state: codes 1 to 7 and 9: all control outputs and the status signal low, watchdog servicing withheld, then software reset (first two detections) or latch (third); code 8: no safe state by itself, watchdog servicing continues, only the latch at the completion of the third completed code 8 report (the code 8 count advances only at report completion)
attributes.reentrancy: callable from task and interrupt context; the read-modify-write of SWC-SUP-054 runs in the short critical section of DEC-SWC-007
attributes.memory: eight history entries (code, entity id, 32 bit time stamp), nine counts, latch, fault count, fault-free time accumulator; static, in the retained region (OP-SWC-003)
attributes.rationale: Code 8 count and latch both taken at the report event to match SWR-LAT-004 and SWR-LAT-012 (a code 8 is counted when its report is made at start-up); an interrupted report advances nothing, so the latch cannot be set after fewer than three completed code 8 reports.

items.name: Safe-state output control
items.description: Static: driver-interface-facing service; the only owner of the GPIO resource for the two control outputs and the status signal, through the GPIO driver interface SWC-SUP-020. Provides SWC-SUP-036. Dynamic: init call from SWC-SUP-002 as the first start-up step configures all three pins as outputs driven low (the pin state between reset and that call is not relied on by this architecture, see OP-SWC-006); the fault manager calls the safe-state command, which first sets a safe-state-commanded flag owned by this component and then drives all three low immediately, and keeps them low while the latch is set (including after software and watchdog resets, because the call at start-up repeats and nothing else drives them high); the status signal is driven high only by the explicit call of the start-up manager after both integrity checks passed, no fault was detected since reset and the latch is clear; the high request is refused (error code, pins unchanged) when the safe-state-commanded flag is set or the fault state interface SWC-SUP-032 reports a fault or the latch. Ordering (DEC-SWC-010): the status-high request performs the flag check, the SWC-SUP-032 read and the status pin write inside one short critical section (interrupts masked, bounded, no waiting, no blocking call inside it), and the safe-state command sets the flag and writes the pins inside the same critical section when called from task context (from interrupt context it cannot be preempted by the task). An interrupt-context safe-state command therefore either completes before the critical section is entered, so the request sees the flag and is refused, or runs after the section ends, so it drives the status pin low after the high write; no interleaving leaves the status pin high after the command. The control outputs are never driven high by the supervisor (the application is outside the architecture).

attributes.access: pins and the safe-state-commanded flag written by this component only; safe-state command callable from task and interrupt context; the status-high request is a protected read-modify-write (flag check, fault state read, pin write) in one critical section; atomicity of an individual pin write is not assumed (OP-SWC-006)
attributes.clock_reset_dependency: GPIO port clock enabled by the driver interface before the first pin configuration; the pin state from reset until the init call is not relied on (OP-SWC-006)
attributes.rationale: F-sw-arch-item-r1-008 and r1-012: ordering by critical section instead of pin-write atomicity; hardware properties not cited, recorded as OP-SWC-006

items.name: Watchdog service
items.description: Static: service layer; the only owner of the independent watchdog (own clock, 100 ms timeout) and the window watchdog resources, through the driver interfaces SWC-SUP-021 and SWC-SUP-022, and of the inhibit flag SWC-SUP-055. Provides SWC-SUP-035. Dynamic: (a) Start-up: the independent watchdog is activated by the start-up manager through this component; start-up services it at chunk boundaries of the integrity-check CRC runs so that activation-to-first-service, consecutive-service and last-service-to-end-of-start-up intervals are each below 100 ms (DEC-SWC-004); the window watchdog is not enabled during start-up (DEC-SWC-005), so no window-watchdog refresh is due in start-up. (b) Operation: the control-cycle task SWC-SUP-061 calls the cycle service at a fixed phase of each control cycle after the flow check; it enables the window watchdog on the first control cycle at that phase (the enabling instant is treated as the previous refresh) and refreshes it once per later cycle at the same phase, so consecutive intervals and the first interval after enabling equal one control period of 10 ms (inside the 6 ms to 12 ms window) and the independent watchdog is serviced in the same call while every supervised task is healthy and no fault has been detected since the last reset. (c) After a detection the inhibit flag is set (called by the fault manager) and neither watchdog is serviced or refreshed until the next reset. The refresh decision is taken in this one place and depends only on supervisor state (health from SWC-SUP-006 and SWC-SUP-007, the inhibit flag), never on data supplied by application tasks, so an application fault cannot cause a refresh. (d) Synchronisation against a detection during a service call (SWR-WDG-001): every service and refresh call (start-up service, cycle service, window-watchdog enable and refresh) executes as one non-interruptible critical section in which interrupts that can set the inhibit flag (the fault-detection path through SWC-SUP-035) are masked on the single core. Inside the section the call reads the inhibit flag SWC-SUP-055 and, only if it is clear, issues the driver-interface service or refresh command (SWC-SUP-021 or SWC-SUP-022), then leaves the section; the check and the command are not separable by an interrupt. A detection raised from interrupt context while the section is open is held pending by the interrupt mask and takes effect when the section ends, so the flag is set before any later call and that call, on its own check, issues nothing; a refresh already issued inside the section is ordered before the detection and is the last one. No watchdog command is issued outside the section and none after the flag is seen set. The inhibit set itself stays atomic and is never masked, so the section delays it by at most the bounded section length; the section contains no waiting and no calls other than the check and the single driver-interface command, and its worst-case length is at most 20 us and part of the budget of the calling task (DEC-SWC-013). The flag is write-once-until-reset, so a later reset is the only way the check can read clear again. Timeout 100 ms and window 6 ms to 12 ms are configured by this component at initialisation.

attributes.safe_state: no refresh -> independent watchdog reset (and window watchdog reset when the hardware does so, OP-SWR-001)
attributes.access: inhibit flag is write-once-until-reset (set by the fault manager, never cleared by software), atomic
attributes.synchronisation: check of the inhibit flag and the watchdog service or refresh command form one critical section with fault-detection interrupts masked; a detection during the section takes effect after it; no command is issued after the flag is seen set
attributes.clock_reset_dependency: independent watchdog runs from its own clock; window watchdog clock enabled by the driver interface before enabling
attributes.rationale: Closes the mechanism choice of OP-SWR-001 by DEC-SWC-004 and DEC-SWC-005; the hardware behaviour of the first refresh after enabling stays open (OP-SWR-001) and is covered conservatively by treating the enabling instant as the previous refresh.

items.name: Diagnostic communication
items.description: Static: application layer; the only owner of the USART resource (115200 baud, 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit) through SWC-SUP-024, and of the transmit queue and request buffer SWC-SUP-056. Provides SWC-SUP-039. Uses SWC-SUP-032 (state, count, history) and SWC-SUP-034 (millisecond count). Dynamic: runs in the diagnostic service task SWC-SUP-063. Transmits, as lines ending with a line feed, RST,<cause> (within 10 ms of the classification instant) and FLT,<code>,<entity>,<ms since start> (within 10 ms of detection; one per control cycle for code 4; the entity per fault code is: task name for codes 1, 2 and 3, none for code 4 beyond its expected task, CODE for 5 and 7, CONFIG for 6 and 9, IWDG or WWDG for 8); <ms since start> is the unsigned 32 bit decimal millisecond count since the latest reset, taken at the instant of detection (for code 8 at the classification instant) and wrapping after 4294967295. The RST line precedes a code 8 line at start-up. A fault report that has no complete transmission before a watchdog reset needs no replay. Requests: a line is received when its terminating line feed arrives; GET STATUS -> STS,<state>,<fault count>; GET FAULTS -> the most recent eight reports made before the instant of reception and since the last power-on reset, oldest first, then END (END only if none; a report made later is not a line of that answer); GET RESET -> RST,<cause>; any other line or one longer than 32 ASCII characters -> ERR; a request received while an answer is transmitted is ignored. Each answer line is at most 40 characters including the line feed, and the answer completes within 50 ms of the terminating line feed, extended by the transmission time of the fault reports sent between request and answer. A fault report due after a request and before the first answer character is sent before that character; one due during an answer line is sent after that line's line feed and before any further answer line. After each completed fault report it notifies the fault manager through SWC-SUP-039. A blocking wait on the USART is not used: every transmit and receive step is non-blocking and bounded by the task period.

attributes.memory: request line buffer 33 characters (32 plus terminator check), answer line buffer 40 characters, report queue sized for the reports of one 10 ms control cycle plus one per fault code; history copy of eight entries for the answer snapshot; all static
attributes.reentrancy: report submission callable from task and interrupt context (queue write in the critical section of DEC-SWC-007); line processing in task context only

items.name: Time service
items.description: Static: service layer; owner of the timer resource (time base and compare events) through the timer driver interface SWC-SUP-023. Provides SWC-SUP-034. Uses nothing else. Dynamic: free-running time base started by the start-up manager before the first release; delivers (a) a time value with a unit of 10 us (DEC-SWC-012; at least the 100 us resolution required for the start-delay and execution-time measurements), (b) the milliseconds since the latest reset as an unsigned 32 bit value wrapping to 0 after 4294967295, (c) the 10 ms control tick, and (d) compare events at requested instants that call the timer event handler task SWC-SUP-062. The elapsed time handed to the fault manager is never larger than the real elapsed time (no over-count).

attributes.access: time base read-only to all callers; compare channel set by this component only; reads are atomic with respect to the tick
attributes.clock_reset_dependency: timer clock enabled by the driver interface; counter restarts at every reset (ms count since the latest reset)

items.name: Fault-injection test hook
items.description: Static: service layer, compiled in test builds only and absent from the production build (verified by inspection of the production build). Provides SWC-SUP-040. Dynamic: called by the test environment on the Renode simulator or host unit tests; each call injects one fault class of fault code 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 or 9 by presenting the corresponding detection condition to the detector concerned (it never calls the fault manager directly except for the code 8 reset-cause injection, which substitutes the reset-flag reading), so that the same detection, reaction and report path is exercised as in a real fault. It owns no hardware resource.

items.name: GPIO driver interface
items.description: Driver interface to the GPIO peripheral for the two control output pins and the status signal pin: configure a pin as output with an initial low level, set a pin level, read back a pin level. No component other than SWC-SUP-009 calls it. Hardware is reached only through it; a host fake or the Renode platform stands behind it in tests.

attributes.data: pin id (control output 1, control output 2, status signal), direction, level
attributes.range: pin id in the three configured pins; level low or high
attributes.timing: each call completes in bounded time, no waiting
attributes.error_behaviour: invalid pin id -> error code, no pin changed

items.name: Independent watchdog driver interface
items.description: Driver interface to the independent watchdog: configure the 100 ms timeout from its own clock, activate it, service it. Called only by SWC-SUP-010.

attributes.error_behaviour: configuration refused -> error code and no activation (reported as a start-up fault by the caller)

items.name: Window watchdog driver interface
items.description: Driver interface to the window watchdog: configure the window so that a refresh earlier than 6 ms or later than 12 ms after the previous one resets, enable it, refresh it. Called only by SWC-SUP-010.

attributes.data: window lower and upper limit, enable, refresh command
attributes.range: lower 6 ms, upper 12 ms after the previous refresh
attributes.error_behaviour: configuration refused -> error code and no enable (reported as a start-up fault by the caller)

items.name: Timer driver interface
items.description: Driver interface to the timer: start the time base, read the counter, arm and cancel a compare event at a counter value, acknowledge the event; the events call the handler of the timer event task SWC-SUP-062 and the 10 ms control tick. Called only by SWC-SUP-012.

attributes.timing: read in bounded time without waiting; compare event armed one unit after the limit expiry; latency to the end of the decision at most 50 us for one event and at most 85 us for coincident events (SWC-SUP-062, DEC-SWC-017)
attributes.error_behaviour: compare value already passed -> event raised immediately

items.name: USART driver interface
items.description: Driver interface to the USART at 115200 baud, 8 data bits, no parity and 1 stop bit: configure, non-blocking transmit of a character or buffer with a count of characters accepted, non-blocking receive of available characters, transmit-complete indication. Called only by SWC-SUP-011.

attributes.timing: no call waits; transmit takes about 87 us per character at the configured rate (derived from the baud rate)
attributes.error_behaviour: transmit full -> fewer characters accepted, none lost silently; receive error -> character dropped and line discarded (answered with ERR when completed)

items.name: Reset control driver interface
items.description: Driver interface to the reset and clock control: read the reset flags set by the latest reset (power-on, independent watchdog, window watchdog, software, other), clear the flags, request a software reset. Called only by SWC-SUP-002; the fault manager reaches it through SWC-SUP-038.

attributes.range: flags: power-on, independent watchdog, window watchdog, software, other
attributes.timing: no waiting; the reset request does not return

items.name: Retained storage driver interface
items.description: Driver interface to the storage that survives software and watchdog resets and is cleared at a power-on reset, holding the retained fault state SWC-SUP-054: read it, write it, clear it, and report whether the content is valid. Validity is a property of the content only and is never interpreted here as a power-on indication. Called only by SWC-SUP-008. The medium is not identified by the inputs (OP-SWC-003). Dynamic: at start-up SWC-SUP-008 combines the validity with the reset cause it obtains from SWC-SUP-002 (reset flags read through SWC-SUP-025). (a) Confirmed power-on reset flag set: the caller clears latch, detection counts and fault history through the clear operation (SWR-LAT-009) and starts with a valid empty state. (b) Any other reset cause (software, independent watchdog, window watchdog, other) with valid content: the content is kept unchanged and used as is (SWR-LAT-007, SWR-LAT-013, SWR-LAT-014); no clear is issued. (c) Any other reset cause with invalid content: no clear is issued and no power-on state is assumed; the retained state cannot be trusted, so the caller enters the latched safe state (the latch is set, which is the conservative state for SWR-LAT-007), keeps the content readable for diagnosis without overwriting entries that still pass their individual check, and records the loss as a fault in the history rather than silently starting empty. The clear operation is accepted only on the caller's confirmed power-on path.

attributes.data: latch, nine detection counts, eight history entries, fault count
attributes.range: survives software and watchdog resets; cleared at power-on reset
attributes.error_behaviour: content not valid -> reported as invalid, never treated as power-on state; after a non-power-on reset the caller keeps the content, sets the latch and records the loss; clear is issued only after a confirmed power-on reset flag
attributes.reentrancy: callable from task and interrupt context under the critical section of DEC-SWC-007

items.name: Task release and checkpoint interface
items.description: Interface between the scheduler SWC-SUP-005, the supervision components SWC-SUP-006 and SWC-SUP-007 and the application tasks: release of a task, start and completion events from the task, one checkpoint per task execution. The tasks have no other path into the supervisor: no watchdog refresh, no output control, no access to supervisor data.

attributes.data: task index, release, start, completion, checkpoint id
attributes.timing: release per the configured period and order; events handled within the budget of the caller
attributes.error_behaviour: out-of-range task index -> error code, no state change
attributes.reentrancy: task context; start and completion events may also arrive from the timer event handler context

items.name: Fault notification interface
items.description: Interface by which every detector (SWC-SUP-001, SWC-SUP-002, SWC-SUP-004, SWC-SUP-006, SWC-SUP-007) hands a detected fault to the fault manager SWC-SUP-008: fault code 1 to 9, entity, instant of detection. The fault manager is the only receiver.

attributes.range: code 1..9; entity per the code (task index, CODE, CONFIG, IWDG, WWDG)
attributes.timing: synchronous call, completes in bounded time; the safe-state command is issued inside it
attributes.error_behaviour: code outside 1..9 -> error code, treated as a configuration fault code 9
attributes.reentrancy: task and interrupt context; serialised by the critical section of DEC-SWC-007

items.name: Fault state interface
items.description: Read-only interface from the fault manager: supervisor state (STARTUP, OPERATIONAL, SAFE, LATCHED), latch, fault count since the last power-on reset, history snapshot of at most eight entries oldest first as of the instant of the request. Used by the scheduler, the output control and diagnostic communication.

attributes.data: state, latch flag, fault count, history entries (code, entity, ms)
attributes.range: history 0..8 entries; LATCHED takes priority over the other states
attributes.timing: snapshot taken in one critical section, fixed as of the call

items.name: CRC value interface
items.description: Interface to the CRC engine SWC-SUP-003: initialise a context to 0xFFFFFFFF, update it with a byte range given as start address and length, read the value. Used by the start-up manager (whole ranges in chunks) and the run-time checker (one segment per call).

attributes.data: context (one 32 bit value), byte range, CRC-32/MPEG-2 value
attributes.range: polynomial 0x04C11DB7, initial value 0xFFFFFFFF, no reflection, no final XOR; bytes in increasing address order; range length 0 to 1 MiB
attributes.timing: time proportional to the range length; callers bound the length per call
attributes.error_behaviour: null range or zero length -> context unchanged

items.name: Time service interface
items.description: Interface provided by SWC-SUP-012: read the time with 100 us resolution, read the milliseconds since the latest reset, request a compare event at a time, and the elapsed-time reading used for fault-free time.

attributes.data: time in 100 us units, millisecond count, event request
attributes.range: ms count unsigned 32 bit wrapping to 0 after 4294967295; 100 us time value wide enough for the longest limit (20 ms) plus margin
attributes.error_behaviour: event request in the past -> event raised immediately

items.name: Watchdog control interface
items.description: Interface provided by the watchdog service SWC-SUP-010: activate the independent watchdog, start-up service, cycle service (called once per control cycle), and inhibit (called by the fault manager on a detection, irreversible until reset).

attributes.range: cycle service once per 10 ms control cycle
attributes.error_behaviour: service after inhibit -> no refresh, no error (silently withheld by design)
attributes.reentrancy: inhibit callable from task and interrupt context (atomic set); services from task context

items.name: Output control interface
items.description: Interface provided by SWC-SUP-009: initialise the three pins (outputs driven low), command the safe state (all three low), request status signal high (accepted only when the checks passed, no fault since reset and the latch is clear).

attributes.timing: bounded, no waiting; safe-state command effective within the call
attributes.error_behaviour: status-high refused -> error code, pins unchanged
attributes.reentrancy: safe-state command callable from interrupt context; init and status-high from task context

items.name: Image and configuration read access
items.description: Read-only access to the memory regions given by the linker symbols __app_start, __app_end (end byte excluded), __app_crc, __cfg_start, __cfg_end (end byte excluded) and __cfg_crc, and the 32 bit little-endian reference words. Provided by the build and the linker (external to the supervisor); no component writes these regions.

endpoints: external: linker-defined image and configuration regions
attributes.range: application image at most 1 MiB; reference words outside the checked ranges
attributes.timing: reads bounded by the range passed
attributes.error_behaviour: end symbol not above start symbol -> treated as a code integrity fault at start-up (code 5) or a configuration integrity fault (code 6)

items.name: Reset request service
items.description: Interface provided by SWC-SUP-002 through which the fault manager requests a software reset; SWC-SUP-002 passes it to the reset control driver interface SWC-SUP-025. Retained state is kept across it.

attributes.range: requested at most within 20 ms after the later of report completion and safe-state entry; never at the third detection of a code 1 to 7 fault
attributes.error_behaviour: request while latch-setting detection is third -> refused by the fault manager before the call

items.name: Report submission interface
items.description: Interface provided by SWC-SUP-011: submit the RST start-up message with a cause, submit a fault report (code, entity, detection instant) and receive a completion notification when the report has been fully transmitted. Used by the start-up manager and the fault manager. Admission: a submission returns ACCEPTED or BUSY and never blocks. Each submitting component keeps one pending cell per report source it owns (one for the RST message, one per fault code 4 to 9, one per supervised task for each of codes 1, 2 and 3) holding code, entity and detection instant; the cell is released only on ACCEPTED, so no report is lost while the queue is full. A BUSY submission is repeated by the submitter on every diagnostic task run (1 ms, SWC-SUP-063) before any newer submission, oldest detection instant first. Pending storage: the report queue in SWC-SUP-056 is a first-in first-out ring with one slot per pending cell (1 + 6 + 3N slots, N the configured supervised task count) plus one slot for the next code 4 report; each slot holds kind, cause or code, entity and detection instant, and the line is rendered from the slot when it is transmitted. With this size BUSY cannot occur in normal operation; it is the defined, bounded fallback, never a drop or an overwrite. Transmission and deadline: the diagnostic task takes slots in queue order (the RST line before an FLT line at start-up; FLT lines in order of admission, which follows detection instant) and hands one line at a time to SWC-SUP-024, never interrupting a line already started. A report line is at most 40 characters including the line feed (about 87 us per character, at most 3.5 ms per line). A report admitted at detection waits at most 1 ms before its first character is handed over: the submission makes the diagnostic task ready at once and, with its priority above the application tasks, its response is bounded at 1 ms whatever the application workload (SWC-SUP-063, DEC-SWC-015); the 1 ms period only covers a BUSY resubmission; the lines ahead of it in the queue are sent first. The k-th queued report therefore completes within 1 ms plus the line times of the k lines up to and including it: within 10 ms of detection for up to two maximum-length lines (7.96 ms), and for more lines when they are shorter (sum of line times at most 9 ms). A line of an answer to a request that is already being sent is completed first (SWC-SUP-011) and can add up to one 40 character line (3.5 ms), so SWR-DIA-001 is met for the reports whose cumulative line time including such a line is at most 9 ms. Guarantee stated at architecture level (DEC-SWC-014): with the default task names (entity at most 6 characters, T_DIAG) an FLT line is at most 24 characters including the line feed, about 2.1 ms; the k-th queued report then completes within 1 ms + (remainder of an answer line in progress, at most 3.5 ms) + k x 2.1 ms of detection. The largest burst the architecture can produce at one instant is four late-start reports (codes 2 of T_IN, T_CTRL, T_OUT and, in a tenth cycle, T_DIAG, all released at the same tick with the same start limit; after the first detection no further task is released): with no answer line in progress the fourth completes within 1 + 4 x 2.1 = 9.4 ms, so SWR-DIA-001 is met for every report; with an answer line in progress the fourth would complete at up to 12.9 ms, which no mechanism on one 115200 baud line can avoid without abandoning a started line, a decision on the interplay of SWR-DIA-001 with a line already started that only a person can make (blocking OP-SWC-013). Reports are in all cases sent in detection order without loss. The completion notification is given to the submitter after the line feed of its report has been handed to the driver and transmit-complete is indicated.

attributes.data: cause, code, entity, instant; completion notification; ACCEPTED/BUSY result
attributes.range: cause POR, IWDG, WWDG, SW, OTHER; code 1..9
attributes.timing: submission non-blocking; admission at submission or on the next 1 ms diagnostic run after BUSY; transmission starts at most 1 ms after admission, one line at most 3.5 ms; the k-th queued report completes within 1 ms plus the line times up to and including it, within 10 ms of detection for cumulative line time at most 9 ms; four default-name reports without an answer line in progress complete within 9.4 ms (DEC-SWC-014); the case with an answer line in progress is OP-SWC-013
attributes.pending_storage: submitter pending cells (1 + 6 + 3N) plus FIFO ring of 1 + 6 + 3N + 1 slots in SWC-SUP-056
attributes.error_behaviour: queue full -> BUSY, the report stays in the submitter's pending cell and is resubmitted every 1 ms run, oldest detection instant first; nothing is dropped and no queued report is overwritten; code or cause outside the range -> error code, nothing queued
attributes.reentrancy: task and interrupt context (queue write in the critical section)
attributes.rationale: Answers F-sw-arch-item-r1-011: bounded admission, pending storage and deadline arithmetic are stated; OP-SWC-007 and OP-SWC-008 hold the values the design closes; OP-SWC-013 holds the decision for a burst while an answer line is in progress.

items.description: Test-build interface by which the test environment injects each fault class of fault codes 1 to 9. Not present in the production build.

attributes.error_behaviour: code outside 1..9 -> error code, nothing injected

items.name: Configuration table
items.description: Table of the four supervised tasks with period, release order, start limit and execution limit (defaults per SWC-SUP-001), held as linker-placed configuration data in the block __cfg_start..__cfg_end protected by its CRC. Owner SWC-SUP-001; all other components read it only.

items.name: Checkpoint log

items.name: Retained fault state

Kept in the retained storage reached through SWC-SUP-026; survives software and watchdog resets; cleared at a power-on reset. Owner SWC-SUP-008.
