attributes.memory: history 8 entries, counts 9, latch, fault count, time accumulators; static

items.name: Watchdog inhibit flag
items.description: Flag set by the fault manager (through SWC-SUP-035) at a detection; while set no watchdog is serviced or refreshed. Cleared only by a reset. Owner SWC-SUP-010.

items.name: Diagnostic queue and buffers
items.description: Report queue (RST and FLT lines with detection instants), request line buffer (32 characters plus a terminator check), answer line buffer (40 characters) and history snapshot of eight entries for the answer in progress. Owner SWC-SUP-011.

attributes.access: queue written from task and interrupt context in the critical section of DEC-SWC-007, read by the diagnostic task; buffers used by the diagnostic task only

items.name: Start-up task
items.description: Execution context that runs once after every reset, before the scheduler is started: executes the start-up manager sequence of SWC-SUP-002 (outputs low, reset classification, RST and code 8, CRC checks in chunks with independent watchdog service between chunks, configuration validation, permission to release). Ends by starting the control tick of SWC-SUP-012 and the 10 ms control-cycle task SWC-SUP-061 when no fault that prevents normal start-up was detected and the latch is clear. A fault code 8 report made at start-up (watchdog reset) is not such a fault: start-up continues after the report (SWR-LAT-011) and the code 8 is counted toward the latch rule when the report is made (SWR-LAT-012); the task does not evaluate the latch, release a task or request status-high until the code 8 report has completed or failed (step 7a of SWC-SUP-002: it keeps driving the transmit step and servicing the independent watchdog while it waits), so a third code 8 report sets the latch before the permission to release; only if that rule, or any other detected fault (for example a failed CRC check or invalid configuration), sets the latch or otherwise prevents normal start-up does the task end in the idle state in which only the diagnostic task SWC-SUP-063 and (until the reset) nothing else runs. Reaching the end with a latch set also means no supervised task is released (SWR-SAF-006). Diagnostic transmission during start-up (DEC-SWC-011): the diagnostic service task SWC-SUP-063 is not running yet, so this task itself drives the transmit step of SWC-SUP-011 (the same non-blocking service step that SWC-SUP-063 calls; the only caller while this task runs, so SWC-SUP-011 and its buffers SWC-SUP-056 have one calling context at any time and SWC-SUP-063 takes over without overlap when it starts). Order: (0) first action, before any other start-up step including reset-cause classification: configure the two control outputs and the status signal as outputs driven low, through the driver interfaces that own them (SWR-SAF-003); (1) classify the reset cause and take the classification instant; (2) immediately, before any CRC chunk or other check, request the RST line from SWC-SUP-011 and, for an independent or window watchdog reset, then request the FLT code 8 line, so the queue holds RST before FLT (first in, first out; SWR-RST-004); (3) call the transmit step of SWC-SUP-011 right after the requests and again between every two CRC chunks and before every independent watchdog service, so a pending report is never left waiting longer than the interval between two calls. Each call moves characters without waiting. The two lines together are at most about 32 characters (RST line at most 10, FLT line for code 8 at most 22 including line feeds), about 87 us per character at 115200 baud, so about 3 ms of transmission; with a call interval of at most 1 ms (the period of SWC-SUP-063) both lines complete well within 10 ms of the classification instant. The chunk size of the CRC checks must therefore also bound the interval between two transmit-step calls to 1 ms; its numeric value is the open point OP-SWC-004 and its execution time per chunk at most 1 ms between two transmit-step calls, with the core clock in OP-SWC-012.

attributes.priority: runs alone before the other tasks are started
attributes.budget_us: runs once, outside the normal-operation window of SWR-RES-001 (the control tick is not running); execution between two transmit-step calls at most 1000 us (DEC-SWC-011, DEC-SWC-013); conversion of the CRC chunk to bytes needs the core clock (OP-SWC-012)
attributes.memory: task stack: no numeric budget (OP-SWC-010, which is a memory open point distinct from the execution-time point OP-SWC-012); stack use is statically bounded because no recursion and no dynamic allocation are allowed (CON-SUP-004); the task has no static data of its own, it uses the state owned by the components it runs
attributes.rationale: Finding F-sw-arch-item-r2-006: memory budget recorded as open point OP-SWC-010 because the inputs give no memory limits
attributes.deadline_ms: independent watchdog service intervals shorter than 100 ms (SWR-WDG-006); RST message and code 8 report (watchdog resets) each complete within 10 ms of the reset classification, RST first; transmit step of SWC-SUP-011 called at least every 1 ms during start-up

items.name: Control-cycle task
items.description: Timer-driven task released by the 10 ms control tick; executes one supervision cycle in two parts separated by one bounded wait, so that the released application tasks run in between. Execution contexts and priority order: (1) timer event handler SWC-SUP-062 (highest, interrupt); (2) this task; (3) the diagnostic task SWC-SUP-063, below this task and above every application task (DEC-SWC-015); (4) the released application tasks of the cycle (T_IN, T_CTRL, T_OUT and, in every tenth cycle, the 100 ms task T_DIAG, in the configured release order of SWC-SUP-050), all below the diagnostic task. Part A (at the tick): scheduler release of the tasks of the cycle (SWC-SUP-005), which only makes them ready and records their release instants; then this task requests from the time service SWC-SUP-012 one compare event at the cycle-end instant (phase OP-SWC-002 after the tick) and waits for it, which ends this task's execution and is the scheduling point at which the released tasks, being the only ready tasks below it, execute in release order (T_DIAG after T_OUT in the tenth cycle) and each report its checkpoint through SWC-SUP-030. Part B (at the cycle-end instant): the compare event enters the timer event handler SWC-SUP-062, which makes this task ready again; as the higher priority it preempts any application task still running, then runs in this order: end-of-cycle program flow check (SWC-SUP-007), run-time integrity segment (SWC-SUP-004, at most 500 us), fault-free time update (SWC-SUP-008), then the watchdog cycle service (SWC-SUP-010) at that same fixed phase OP-SWC-002 so that refresh instants are one period apart. Ordering constraint: the cycle-end instant (phase OP-SWC-002, inside the 10 ms cycle and before the 12 ms window watchdog limit) lies after the execution-limit expiry of the 10 ms tasks T_IN, T_CTRL and T_OUT of that cycle (default limit 3 ms each, CON-SUP-103), so such a task that completes within its limit has reported its checkpoint before the flow check; one that has not completed by then is already detected by the timing supervision (SWC-SUP-006) or is reported by the flow check as a missing checkpoint (fault code 4). This ordering does not hold for T_DIAG in the tenth cycle: its default execution limit is 20 ms (CON-SUP-103), longer than the 10 ms cycle, so the limit expiry cannot precede the cycle end and a T_DIAG that is still within its limit may not have reported its checkpoint at the cycle-end flow check. The architecture does not invent how the flow check treats such a T_DIAG (missing checkpoint at the cycle end as SWR-FLW-001 reads literally, or evaluated at the end of the cycle in which its limit expires); this is recorded as open point OP-SWC-011 and the flow-check step stays at the cycle end for every task. The numeric phase is the design parameter of OP-SWC-002. Timeout path of the wait: the wait is bounded by that compare event; if it is lost or late, part B does not run, no watchdog refresh follows and the window watchdog expires at 12 ms after the previous refresh (SWR-WDG-004). The watchdog service is reached only when the previous steps raised no fault since the last reset. In normal operation the supervisor stays within 10 % of the processor time over any 1 s window.

attributes.priority: highest task priority below the timer event handler
attributes.budget_detail: per 10 ms cycle: part A (release, arming start-limit events) 100 us, part B without the run-time check (flow check, fault-free time, watchdog cycle service) 90 us, run-time check segment 500 us (SWR-CHK-008); total 690 us; allocation within the supervisor total of DEC-SWC-013 (920 us per cycle, 9.2 % against the 10 % of SWR-RES-001)
attributes.deadline_ms: end of each cycle, before the window watchdog upper limit of 12 ms after the previous refresh
attributes.memory: task stack: no numeric budget (OP-SWC-010, the memory open point, distinct from the execution-time point OP-SWC-012); stack use is statically bounded because no recursion and no dynamic allocation are allowed (CON-SUP-004), by the deepest call chain of the runs list; the task owns no static data, it uses the state owned by the components it runs; the numeric stack budget is set in the detailed design from the call graph and the device memory size
attributes.wait_point: after the release of SWC-SUP-005, until the cycle-end compare event of SWC-SUP-012 at phase OP-SWC-002; the released application tasks run during the wait
attributes.rationale: Finding F-sw-arch-item-r1-006: the flow check needs the checkpoints of the released tasks, which can only run while this higher-priority task waits; the budget_us of 690 covers part A, part B and the run-time check, not the wait.

items.name: Timer event handler
items.description: Interrupt-triggered execution context entered by the timer compare events armed by SWC-SUP-012 at the start-limit and execution-limit expiry of every released task (and by the cycle tick); runs the limit comparison of SWC-SUP-006 and, on a detection, the fault manager reaction. It is the highest-priority context so that a late-start or overrun fault is detected within 100 us after the limit expires, independent of the 10 ms task period. Coincident events (DEC-SWC-017): one entry decides every compare event that is due or falls due during the pass (up to 2N = 8 limit events for N = 4 tasks, plus the cycle-end event taken last); the safe-state reaction runs once, at the first detection, and each further decision is at most 5 us, so the last limit event is decided at most 85 us after the compare instant and the whole pass is at most 90 us.

attributes.period_ms: event driven, up to one start and one execution event per released task per period
attributes.budget_detail: single event: at most 50 us from the compare instant to the end of the decision (20 us wait for a critical section, 10 us entry and exit, 20 us first decision with the fault reaction), detection at most 60 us after the limit expires with the 10 us unit (SWC-SUP-006, DEC-SWC-012); coincident events (DEC-SWC-017): each further decision at most 5 us, last of eight limit events decided at most 20 + 10 + 20 + 7 x 5 = 85 us after the compare instant, detection at most 95 us after expiry, whole pass including the cycle-end event at most 90 us; in normal operation one entry per cycle (cycle-end event), 50 us per cycle (DEC-SWC-013); the values are allocations conditional on the clock of OP-SWC-012

items.name: Diagnostic service task
items.description: Periodic task that runs the diagnostic communication SWC-SUP-011: moves queued report and answer characters to the USART without waiting, assembles received request lines, and answers requests. The 1 ms period is a decision (DEC-SWC-008): it lets a report be transmitted within 10 ms of detection and an answer within 50 ms. Scheduling (DEC-SWC-015): the task has a priority above every application task and below the control-cycle task SWC-SUP-061 and the timer event handler SWC-SUP-062, so the permitted application workload (execution limits of up to 3 ms for the 10 ms tasks and 20 ms for T_DIAG) cannot delay it. It is also made ready at once by every report submission (SWC-SUP-039), in addition to its 1 ms period. Response bound from the ready instant to the first character handed to the USART driver, including the coincident compare events of DEC-SWC-017: at most 0.8 ms of higher-priority work (control-cycle part B 590 us; handler work for the largest event set in the window, which is all eight limit events of N = 4 tasks plus the cycle-end event, each in its own entry (the worst case, no sharing of an entry), first entry 30 us and each further entry 10 us entry plus 5 us decision, 30 + 7 x 15 + 15 = 150 us; one critical section 20 us; total 760 us, rounded up; no further higher-priority work exists) plus at most 0.2 ms for the task's own transmit step, in total at most 1 ms. The 1 ms first-character bound used in SWC-SUP-039 therefore holds for any application workload and for the maximum coincident interrupt workload; the allocations are conditional on the clock of OP-SWC-012. Service-answer deadline for that workload: a request answer of at most eight 40 character lines needs at most about 28 ms of line time, so with the 1 ms first-character bound the unextended answer completes within about 29 ms of the line feed of the request, leaving 21 ms of the 50 ms limit; the extension by fault reports sent between request and answer (CON-SUP-139) is at most the largest burst the architecture can produce, four default-name reports of about 2.1 ms each (DEC-SWC-014), 8.4 ms, which fits that margin (29 + 8.4 = 37.4 ms). Because the task preempts application tasks only while a report or answer is being transmitted, which is not normal operation (SWR-RES-001), its active execution is not part of the normal-operation allocation; whether such preemption counts in a task's measured execution time is OP-SWC-016.

attributes.priority: below the control-cycle task SWC-SUP-061 and above every application task (DEC-SWC-015)
attributes.response_ms: ready instant to first character at most 1 ms (0.8 ms higher-priority interference including coincident compare events, DEC-SWC-017, plus 0.2 ms own step), independent of application workload
attributes.budget_detail: per 1 ms run at most 10 us when idle (no request, no report), 100 us per 10 ms cycle (DEC-SWC-013); transmission work of a report or answer is not normal operation (SWR-RES-001)

decisions.text: All peripherals are reached only through the driver interfaces SWC-SUP-020 to SWC-SUP-026; no component touches a register, and every peripheral has exactly one owning component (GPIO SWC-SUP-009, independent and window watchdog SWC-SUP-010, timer SWC-SUP-012, USART SWC-SUP-011, reset control SWC-SUP-002, retained storage SWC-SUP-008).
decisions.rationale: Host unit tests and Renode runs need fakes behind the interfaces (SWR-TST-002) and freedom from interference needs a single writer per resource.

decisions.text: Every fault is handed to the fault manager (SWC-SUP-008) which commands the safe state inside the detector's call.
decisions.rationale: The safe-state reaction within 49 ms (SWR-SAF-001), the watchdog inhibit (SWR-WDG-001) and the report must follow one order and one decision point for all fault codes.

decisions.text: The watchdog refresh decision is taken in one place (SWC-SUP-010) and application tasks have no interface that can refresh a watchdog, drive an output or write supervisor data (SWC-SUP-030 carries only release, start, completion and checkpoint).
decisions.rationale: Freedom from interference: an application fault must not cause a refresh (SWR-WDG-004, SWR-WDG-005). The enforcement against direct access by application code is a system-level constraint (OP-SYE-008) and not decided here.

decisions.text: During start-up the CRC runs over the image and the configuration block are cut into chunks and the independent watchdog is serviced between chunks, so that activation-to-first-service, consecutive-service and last-service-to-end-of-start-up intervals stay below 100 ms with margin (chunk size in OP-SWC-004).
decisions.rationale: Closes the mechanism choice left to sw-arch in OP-SWR-001 for the independent watchdog (SWR-WDG-006): a 1 MiB check in one call could exceed the 100 ms timeout.

decisions.text: The window watchdog is enabled at the fixed phase of the first control cycle (not during start-up) and refreshed once per cycle at the same phase, so the first interval after enabling and every later interval are one control period (10 ms) apart.
decisions.rationale: Closes the mechanism choice of OP-SWR-001 for the window watchdog: no window refresh is due while the integrity checks run (SWR-WDG-007 to SWR-WDG-011 hold vacuously or with the 10 ms interval), the enabling instant is treated as the previous refresh (SWR-WDG-012), and 10 ms lies inside the 6 ms to 12 ms window (SWR-WDG-003, SWR-WDG-008).

decisions.text: The CRC-32/MPEG-2 value is computed in software by SWC-SUP-003; the CRC peripheral is not used.
decisions.rationale: CON-SUP-003 names the peripheral but not its algorithms, and the required CRC (SWR-CHK-001, SWR-CHK-003) is fixed; a software computation also runs on host and Renode.

decisions.text: Data shared between task and interrupt context (SWC-SUP-051, SWC-SUP-052, SWC-SUP-054, SWC-SUP-056) is changed only inside a short critical section with bounded length; shared flags are single atomic words.
decisions.rationale: Protects read-modify-write sequences between the timer event handler and the cycle and diagnostic tasks and keeps the detection latency bounded (SWR-TIM-001, SWR-TIM-002); no dynamic memory, no recursion (SWR-PLT-003, SWR-PLT-004).

decisions.text: The diagnostic service task runs every 1 ms without blocking waits.
decisions.rationale: A fault report must start within 10 ms of detection (SWR-DIA-001) and answers complete within 50 ms (SWR-SVC-014); a transmit of a 40 character line takes about 3.5 ms at 115200 baud, so a longer period would leave too little margin.

decisions.text: During start-up the start-up task SWC-SUP-060 calls the transmit step of SWC-SUP-011 itself, right after queueing RST (and the code 8 line) and between CRC chunks, at least every 1 ms; SWC-SUP-063 takes over after start-up.
decisions.rationale: SWR-RST-002 and SWR-RST-003 require both lines within 10 ms of the classification, while start-up checks run alone before the other tasks; one caller at a time keeps SWC-SUP-011 ownership of the USART and queue unchanged, and the FIFO queue keeps RST before code 8 (SWR-RST-004).

decisions.text: The run-time code check advances one 1 KiB segment per control cycle from the control-cycle task, with one CRC context carried across the segments of a pass.
decisions.rationale: Meets 0.5 ms per cycle (SWR-CHK-008) and 1 MiB in about 10.24 s (SWR-CHK-011) and gives one whole-range value (SWR-CHK-007).

decisions.text: The time base of SWC-SUP-012 has a unit of 10 us; each limit compare event is armed one unit after the limit expiry (release or start instant + limit + 10 us) and the handler latency to the end of the decision is at most 50 us for one event and at most 85 us for coincident events (DEC-SWC-017).
decisions.rationale: Detection at most 60 us (single event) or 95 us (eight coincident events) after the configured limit expires (SWR-TIM-001, SWR-TIM-002) while a value equal to the limit stays within it (SWR-TIM-003, SWR-TIM-004); a 100 us unit with an event one unit after expiry would leave no latency budget.

decisions.text: Normal-operation execution allocation per 10 ms cycle (SWR-RES-001, 10 % = 1000 us): control-cycle task SWC-SUP-061 690 us (part A 100, part B 90, run-time check 500), timer event handler SWC-SUP-062 50 us (one cycle-end entry), diagnostic task SWC-SUP-063 100 us (ten idle runs of 10 us), start, completion and checkpoint event handling inside the application tasks 80 us; total 920 us, 9.2 %, margin 80 us. Critical sections of DEC-SWC-007 and of the watchdog service are at most 20 us. The control-cycle part B (590 us at most plus preemption by SWC-SUP-062) finishes inside the 10 ms cycle, before the 12 ms window of SWR-WDG-004.
decisions.rationale: SWR-RES-001 caps the supervisor at 10 % over any 1 s window and SWR-CHK-008 allows 500 us for the run-time check; the allocation shows the parts fit; the values are targets measured on the simulator at the configured core clock (OP-SWC-012), whose feasibility condition (minimum clock for the 500 us CRC segment) is DEC-SWC-016; start-up is outside normal operation.

decisions.text: Report deadline guarantee: the k-th queued report completes within 1 ms + answer-line remainder (at most 3.5 ms) + the line times of the k reports; the architecture-bound burst of four default-name late-start reports meets 10 ms (9.4 ms) when no answer line is in progress.
decisions.rationale: SWR-DIA-001 requires every fault report within 10 ms; the single 115200 baud line serialises reports, so the guarantee is a computed bound, not a claim for unbounded bursts.

decisions.text: Scheduling and configuration granularity. (a) The diagnostic task SWC-SUP-063 has a priority above every application task and below SWC-SUP-061 and SWC-SUP-062, and is made ready at once by each report submission as well as every 1 ms; its response to the first character is at most 1 ms (0.8 ms interference including coincident compare events, DEC-SWC-017, and 0.2 ms own step). (b) A configured period is a whole number (at least one) of 10 ms ticks within the scheduler's tick counter width; any other period is rejected at start-up as configuration fault code 9.
decisions.rationale: (a) With the diagnostic task below the application tasks, three 3 ms tasks or a 20 ms T_DIAG could delay it past the 1 ms the report (SWR-DIA-001) and answer (SWR-SVC-014) arithmetic assumes; raising it bounds the delay by supervisor work only. (b) The scheduler runs on the 10 ms tick (CON-SUP-006), so a period that is not a tick multiple cannot be released as configured; rejecting it as out of range keeps SWR-CFG-007 and SWR-CFG-008 true without inventing a rounding rule.

decisions.text: The execution allocations of DEC-SWC-013 are time allocations, not demonstrated budgets: no feasibility is claimed for them because the inputs give neither the core clock nor the CRC throughput. Condition under which they hold, with f the core clock in MHz and c the cycles per byte of the software CRC loop of SWC-SUP-003: the run-time CRC segment needs 1024 x c <= 500 x f, and every other allocation needs its instruction count at most its time times f (part A 100 us = 100 x f cycles, part B 90 us, handler single entry 50 us and coincident pass 90 us, diagnostic 100 us, event handling 80 us, together 420 us per cycle = 420 x f cycles, outside the CRC segment). Neither c nor the instruction counts are established by any input or measurement, so no value of c or f is assumed here; the value of 10 cycles per byte (about 21 MHz) is only an illustration of the arithmetic and is not relied on. The segment size cannot be shortened below about 960 bytes without breaking the 11 s pass limit (SWR-CHK-008, SWR-CHK-011), so the clock, not the segment, absorbs a slower CRC loop.
decisions.rationale: States the architecture-level condition under which SWR-CHK-008 and SWR-RES-001 are achievable without supplying a clock or throughput the inputs do not give. The configured core clock is a platform decision only a person can make (OP-SWC-012, blocking); until it is made and the instruction counts are demonstrated at that configuration, the allocations are not relied on as feasible, and if the confirmed clock is too low the clock or the requirement has to change.

decisions.text: Coincident compare events: the timer event handler SWC-SUP-062 is one pass that decides every compare event due or falling due during the pass, in expiry order, equal instants in configured release order with start-limit events before execution-limit events, and takes the cycle-end event last. The fault reaction (outputs low, watchdog inhibit) runs at the first detection only; each further decision is at most 5 us. At most 2N = 8 limit events (N = 4, capacity of SWC-SUP-051) can be pending at once, so the last is decided at most 20 + 10 + 20 + 7 x 5 = 85 us after the compare instant and detected at most 95 us after its limit expires (10 us unit plus 85 us), within 100 us. The diagnostic task response (SWC-SUP-063) is recomputed for the same workload: 0.8 ms interference plus 0.2 ms own step.
decisions.rationale: Closes F-sw-arch-set-r3-003 and r3-005: the earlier bound assumed a single handler entry. The 5 us, 10 us and 20 us values are allocations that depend on the clock of OP-SWC-012, as in DEC-SWC-016.

decisions.text: SWC-SUP-009 serialises the status-high request (flag check, fault state read, status pin write) and the safe-state command with a short bounded critical section and a safe-state-commanded flag it owns.
decisions.rationale: Atomic individual pin writes do not stop an interrupt-context safe-state command between the check and the write; the critical section and flag guarantee the status pin is never left high after a fault or latch (SWR-SAF-001, SWR-SAF-004).

open_points.text: The core clock is not given (SWR-RES-001 is measured at the configured core clock). The execution allocations of DEC-SWC-013 are time targets; turning them into instruction counts and the CRC chunk size needs the clock, a configuration value the design and simulator setup close. The architecture-level allocation holds only under the condition of DEC-SWC-016 (1024 x c <= 500 x f for the CRC segment, and the other allocations as instruction counts at f). Neither the clock f nor the CRC throughput c is given or measured, so the architecture cannot state that the budgets are feasible; the decision on the configured core clock (the platform configuration for the Renode runs and the target) is a platform value only a person can give, and the budgets of DEC-SWC-013, DEC-SWC-016 and DEC-SWC-017 are not relied on until it is made. If the confirmed clock is too low, a person must decide between a faster clock and a changed requirement.

Preemption of an application task by the diagnostic task (while a report or answer is transmitted) and by the control-cycle part B lengthens the wall-clock time from start to completion of that task. The inputs do not say whether the execution time measured for SWR-TIM-002 includes such preemption or only the task's own processing. The architecture measures start to completion instants (SWC-SUP-006) and bounds the diagnostic interference per run (0.2 ms), but the treatment is a requirement-level choice.

The phase offset inside the 10 ms control cycle at which the flow check and the watchdog cycle service run, and the numeric priority scheme, are not given by the inputs. The architecture fixes only that the refresh instants are one control period apart and after the flow check; the value is a design parameter.

The inputs name no storage that survives software and watchdog resets but is cleared at a power-on reset (CON-SUP-003 lists none); follows OP-SYE-001. The architecture states the retained fault state SWC-SUP-054 and its driver interface SWC-SUP-026 independent of the medium.

Handling of a non-integral period is closed at architecture level by DEC-SWC-015 (rejected as configuration fault 9 at start-up). What remains is only the numeric upper bound of a period, which is the width of the scheduler's per-entry tick counter and the period encoding of the configuration format; whatever width the design picks, validation uses it, so no accepted value is mistimed.

CON-SUP-002 names RM0486 without a section or page, so no controlled hardware reference supports the GPIO access and reset properties (whether a single pin write is atomic, and the pin state from reset until configuration). SWC-SUP-009 does not rely on either: ordering is by critical section and the init call drives the pins low. The section and page, and any reliance on external pull-downs for the interval before init, are to be fixed in the detailed design.

The CRC throughput at the configured core clock is not stated, so the chunk size that keeps each independent watchdog service interval well below 100 ms (DEC-SWC-004) cannot be fixed here; the margin and chunk size are design values.

The number of characters the USART driver interface SWC-SUP-024 accepts per transmit call (its buffer depth) is not given. The deadline analysis of SWC-SUP-039 assumes a full report line of at most 40 characters is accepted per call or drained without waiting; the depth is a driver design value that must meet this.

The maximum length of a task name used as entity in a fault report is not given. The 40 character report line limit of SWC-SUP-039 requires the configuration to limit the name length; the limit is a configuration design value.

The timer clock and prescaler are not given, so it is not established that the time base can run at the 10 us unit DEC-SWC-012 needs for the 100 us detection bound; the design confirms the unit at the configured clock or a finer unit is used.

SWR-DIA-001 requires every fault report within 10 ms of detection, and a line already started is completed first. If four reports are detected at one instant while an answer line is in progress, the fourth cannot complete within 10 ms (up to 12.9 ms, DEC-SWC-014). Whether such a coincidence is accepted, whether a started answer line may be abandoned, or SWR-DIA-001 is relaxed for it is a requirement-level decision only a person can make.

The inputs give no RAM, flash or stack limit (CON-SUP-004 only forbids dynamic allocation and recursion) and no device memory size, so no numeric stack or other memory budget can be allocated to the start-up task SWC-SUP-060 or to the other tasks. Architecture-level bounds that hold without a number: no dynamic allocation and no recursion (CON-SUP-004), so stack use is statically bounded by the call depth of the runs list; the task owns no shared data. The numeric stack budget is set in the detailed design from the call graph and the device memory size. The same applies to the control-cycle task SWC-SUP-061.

T_DIAG has a default execution limit of 20 ms (CON-SUP-103) but is released in a 10 ms control cycle, and SWR-FLW-001 requires the program flow check at the end of each control cycle for the tasks released in that cycle. A T_DIAG within its limit can therefore not have reported its checkpoint at that cycle end. The inputs do not say whether a not-yet-reported T_DIAG is a flow fault at that cycle end or is evaluated at the end of the cycle in which its execution limit expires. This is a requirement-level decision only a person can make.
